config.theme: Robot Riot email-header banner — same event/cast as the Robot Riot postcard, recomposed as a wide letterboxed 3:1 banner with the League corner logo
config.scene_description: A Robot Riot banner scene composed so ALL content sits within the TOP THIRD of the 1536x1024 canvas (a band roughly 1536x340px along the top edge), as if built for a wide letterboxed crop; the bottom two-thirds of the canvas is a plain, unimportant continuation of the golden-amber arena floor, since it will be cropped away and discarded. Within that top band: the headline ROBOT RIOT runs across the very top in a clean, bold, chunky demolition-derby logo style, signal-red fill with heavy black outline, sized with a clear margin so no letter touches the top edge. Below the headline, ONLY two kid drivers total (not four, not a crowd) — one near the left edge, one near the right edge — lean in gripping joystick controllers, excited and focused, heads and shoulders fully inside the band. At the center of the band, two Cutebot robots (recognizable educational-robotics builds, wheels and attachments like a blade/ramp/gripper/scoop) collide head-on in a flat impact starburst with jagged crack lines, positioned low enough in the band that no part of either robot is cropped by the band's lower edge. In the top-left corner of the full canvas, tucked tight into the corner: the League diagonal corner-banner logo, small, clear of the headline and the left driver.

iterations.prompt:
Golden-Age comic illustration, hand-inked Graphic Novel style (the HisMastersVoice look): bold tapered black ink contours, dense confident pen strokes carrying all the detail, broad flat saturated color fields with crisp hard edges, no gradients, no airbrush, no painted digital shading, no soft glows. Palette: warm-dominant orange-and-blue, roughly 70% warm/30% cool — Golden Amber #F9C233 and Marigold #F9B41E for the big background field, Burnt Orange #C96A10 and Sienna #9A4E12 for warm shadow and modeled form, Steel Blue #175E8C and Deep Navy #16223C only as a cool accent on machine chassis, borders, and deepest shadows, Signal Red #CC1616 used sparingly as a spark for the title only, Ink Black #101010 anchoring every contour, Cream #FBE5A0 for any text furniture. Spend visual detail ONLY on the two kid drivers and the two Cutebot robots — hatching, feathering, wires, bolts, wheel treads rendered stroke by stroke; simplify the arena floor and background into bold flat shapes.

CRITICAL LAYOUT CONSTRAINT: this artwork will be cropped to a 3:1 wide banner by keeping only the TOP THIRD of the canvas and discarding the bottom two-thirds. Therefore compose EVERY important element — headline, kids, robots, corner logo — entirely within a horizontal band occupying the top third of the 1536x1024 canvas (roughly y=0 to y=340px), with comfortable margins so nothing touches the very top edge or the y=340 crop line. The bottom two-thirds of the canvas is simply a plain, unimportant continuation of the golden-amber raised arena floor — no faces, hands, robots, or lettering may extend down into it.

Scene, left to right within that top band: in the top-left corner of the canvas, tucked tight into the corner, the League diagonal corner-banner logo/wordmark — small and fully clear of the headline and the left driver. Then, spanning the width of the band, ONE kid driver leaning in from the left edge gripping a joystick controller (rear view of the controller: battery compartment, mounting bracket, red-and-blue side grips, no invented buttons), excited and focused, head and shoulders entirely inside the band. At the center of the band, two Cutebot robots collide head-on in a small flat impact starburst with jagged black crack lines radiating outward — recognizable educational-robotics builds on wheels, one with a blade or ramp attachment, the other with a gripper or scoop, positioned low enough in the band that no part of either robot is cropped by the y=340 line and high enough to clear the arena rim beneath them. Then a second kid driver leaning in from the right edge, matching the first in energy and controller detail. A raised circular arena with a golden-amber top surface and a low dark spindle rim railing is visible behind/beneath the action, reading clearly as a fight-night ring.

TEXT: across the very top of the band, the headline "ROBOT RIOT" in a clean, bold, chunky demolition-derby logo style, signal-red fill with a heavy black outline, sized with a clear margin on all sides so no letter touches the top edge of the canvas or the y=340 crop line. On the small corner logo, render exactly: "THE LEAGUE OF" / "AMAZING" / "PROGRAMMERS" stacked along the diagonal banner, with the subhead ribbon "SMART MINDS · BOLD IDEAS · BRIGHT FUTURES" running along the ribbon's lower edge — all in small, clean, legible lettering appropriate to its small size. No other lettering, signs, labels, or captions anywhere.
iterations.negative_prompt:
No grain, speckle, stipple, halftone, newsprint, parchment, aged or yellowed paper, print-dot texture, soft airbrush glow. No painted/airbrushed shading, soft gradients, glossy rendered highlights, digital-painting look, rendered 3D volume, or cinematic photo lighting. No photorealism, photographic faces, 3D render, or CGI. No anime/manga cel style, chibi, Funko-Pop, or oversized cartoon heads. No muddy, washed-out, or pastel color — keep fields saturated and flat.

Do NOT put any important content — faces, hands, robot parts, lettering — in the bottom two-thirds of the canvas; that area must stay a plain, empty continuation of the arena floor. Do NOT show more than two kid drivers or more than two robots. Do NOT show a crowd, spectators, or audience. Do NOT let the ROBOT RIOT headline or the corner logo touch any edge of the canvas or bleed past the top-third band. No invented extra posters, signs, slogans, or logos. No weapons, lasers, explosions, or military imagery. No portrait/vertical orientation — landscape only.
iterations.notes: First pass: letterboxed top-third composition so a 3:1 crop captures headline+2 kids+2 robots+corner logo without cutting anything off.
